question.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 0}[3f(t)-g(t)]$ given that
$f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,{t}^{2}-2,\frac{t-3}{{t}^{2}+1}⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\sqrt{t}+\sqrt{2},2⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}({t}^{2}-2),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(\frac{t-3}{{t}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡0,{0}^{2}-2,\frac{0-3}{{0}^{2}+1}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-2,-3⟩ \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(\sqrt{t}+\sqrt{2}),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\sqrt{0}+\sqrt{2},2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\sqrt{2},2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[3f(t)-g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}3f(t)-{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =3{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)-{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =3⟨1,-2,-3⟩-⟨0,\sqrt{2},2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-6,-9⟩-⟨0,\sqrt{2},2⟩ \\  & =⟨3-0,-6-\sqrt{2},-9-2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-6-\sqrt{2},-11⟩\end{aligned}
$$
